_note: Platform-neutral shortcut= accelerator matching. The declaration is parsed once (lowercased, split on '+', trimmed; the last token is the key, the rest are modifiers) and each key event is matched deterministically: cmd is the PRIMARY modifier (Command on Apple, Ctrl elsewhere, so it matches meta OR ctrl); ctrl/alt/shift are literal; the key compares case-insensitively. An UNMODIFIED shortcut (no cmd and no ctrl) never fires while an editable target holds focus, so typing is never stolen. The event's toolkit adapter fills key/meta/ctrl/alt/shift/editable; the shared rule below decides `fires`.

cases.name: cmd+s fires on the meta key (Apple)
cmd+s fires on the ctrl key (non-Apple)
cmd+s does not fire with no primary modifier
modified shortcut still fires inside an editable target
unmodified shortcut is suppressed inside an editable target
unmodified shortcut fires outside an editable target
ctrl-modified shortcut fires inside an editable target
ctrl literal is not satisfied by meta alone
alt modifier is required when declared
alt modifier missing does not fire
shift modifier is required when declared
shift missing does not fire the shift-declared shortcut
declaration whitespace and casing are normalized
